Education / EdTech & online learning

Turn trials into learners who finish what they start

Online learning businesses live on activation, completion and renewal, often with learners under eighteen. We build product analytics, lifecycle messaging, cohort scheduling and grounded support that respect age gates and parental consent, so adult learners get timely nudges, children are not profiled or targeted, and mentors see who needs a person.

The challenge

What makes edtech & online learning different.

01

Many sign-ups never finish the first lesson, and generic email sequences treat a curious visitor and a committed learner the same way.

02

Completion drops after the first modules, and live cohorts lose attendance when reminders arrive at the wrong time or on the wrong channel.

03

Learners under eighteen need verifiable parental consent, and from May 2027, under the notified DPDP Rules, tracking, behavioral monitoring and targeted ads aimed at them are barred unless an exemption applies.

04

Support teams answer the same login, payment, certificate and refund questions all day, while real learning problems wait.

Where automation helps

Practical uses for edtech & online learning.

01

Activation-led trial journeys

Trial users guided to the first lesson, first quiz and first live session, with nudges based on the step they have not reached, for adult learners who opted in.

02

Age gate and parent consent

Sign-up asks for age, routes under-18 accounts to a parent consent step that confirms the parent is an identifiable adult, for example through a DigiLocker token, and switches off behavioral nudges and ad audiences for those accounts.

03

Cohort scheduling and session reminders

Learners placed in live cohorts by time zone, language and timing, with session reminders and recordings sent on the channel each learner chose.

04

Completion and re-engagement

Learners who stall get one reminder tied to their next module, and those who stay inactive are flagged to a mentor instead of receiving more messages.

05

Grounded learner support

Login, billing, certificate and refund questions answered from the help center with citations, and learning or well-being concerns handed to a person.

06

Practice analytics and doubt queues

Quiz and test results summarized by topic for each learner, with doubts queued to subject experts and AI-drafted hints reviewed by them before release.

Visit, demo or trialStandard4–6 weeks

Trial activation and paid conversion for online courses

Product events show which trial learners reached their first lesson, quiz or live session. Adult learners who opted in get nudges tied to their next step, under-18 accounts get service messages to the parent only, and the growth team sees conversion by course and channel.

EdTech & online learning

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Many trial sign-ups never finish a first lesson, and generic drip emails treat every learner the same. Behavior-based nudges suit adults but cannot be applied to children, and countdown pressure or hard-to-cancel trials are dark patterns under the consumer authority's guidelines.

Trigger

A learner starts a free trial or sample course on the website or app, or completes, skips or abandons a key activation step.

How it runs

  • Ask for age at sign-up and route under-18 learners to a parent consent step that checks the parent is an identifiable adult, for example through a DigiLocker token, before the account is activated.
  • Track activation events such as first lesson, first quiz and first live session for adult accounts, and only the service events the course needs for child accounts.
  • Send adult learners who opted in an email or WhatsApp nudge tied to the step they have not reached, from approved templates with weekly caps.
  • For child accounts, send the parent only service messages such as the trial end date, the schedule and how to cancel.
  • Before the trial ends, show the price, renewal terms and a one-click cancel option, and send a reminder before the first charge, separate from the bank's pre-debit notice for recurring payments.
  • Report activation and trial-to-paid conversion by course, cohort and channel, with child accounts excluded from every ad audience.

Human checkpoint

The growth lead approves every sequence, cap and template, and the data protection contact approves the age gate and parent consent flow. Refund and cancellation disputes go to the learner success lead, never to an automated reply.

Systems it connects

  • Payment gateway or app store billing
  • Help center

Data & consent

Adults: email, phone, course and activation events, with a separate marketing opt-in. Under-18s: the parent's identity and consent record, with analytics limited to what the service needs and no ad tracking. Event data is kept for the period stated in the privacy notice, and learners can withdraw consent or delete their account in settings.

What we deliver

  • Age gate and parent consent flow
  • Approved lifecycle sequences with frequency caps
  • Clear renewal and cancellation messages

How we measure it

  • Trial-to-paid conversion
  • Cancellations in the first billing cycle
  • Unsubscribe rate on nudges

Onboard and scheduleStandard3–5 weeks

Batch and cohort allocation with schedule change notices

New students are placed in batches or live cohorts by course, center or time zone, medium and timing within capacity. Faculty availability is checked, timetables are published, and every later change reaches only the affected students and parents.

Coaching & test-prep institutes · EdTech & online learning

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Batches fill unevenly, timing preferences live in spreadsheets, and schedule changes are announced in large groups that students mute. In coaching, timings may also need to respect school hours and daily limits under state coaching rules or the institute's own policy.

Trigger

A student completes enrollment, a batch reaches capacity, or a coordinator changes a class time, room, faculty member or mode.

How it runs

  • Read enrollments with course, center or time zone, medium and preferred timing, and propose placements within room and faculty capacity.
  • Check proposed timetables against the rules the institute sets, such as no classes during school hours, a weekly off and a maximum daily duration.
  • Show the plan to the academic coordinator, who adjusts and approves placements and timetables.
  • Publish each student's batch, timetable and room or joining link in the app, and confirm it to the student and, for minors, the parent.
  • When a class moves, notify only that batch with a one-tap acknowledgment, and re-send to anyone who has not opened it before the class.

Human checkpoint

The academic coordinator approves every placement, batch transfer and timetable change, and faculty confirm their availability. Requests to move a student between batches are decided by the academic head, never by the scheduler.

Tools

Systems it connects

  • Faculty roster

  • Live class tools such as Zoom or Google Meet

Data & consent

Uses name, course, batch, contact numbers and preferred timing. Placement uses course, timing and capacity, not test rankings, and student-facing messages never label batches by performance. Change logs are kept for at least a year to settle disputes, then deleted.

What we deliver

  • Batch and cohort planning board
  • Timetable rule checks agreed with the academic head
  • Change notification flow with acknowledgments
  • Capacity and fill report

How we measure it

  • Change notices acknowledged before class
  • Classes missed after schedule changes
  • Coordinator time spent on scheduling

Attend and learnStandard4–5 weeks

Student and learner helpdesk grounded in the handbook

Students, parents and online learners ask questions on WhatsApp, the portal or the app and get answers cited from the current handbook, fee policy, academic calendar or help center. Grievances, ragging reports and signs of distress go straight to people.

Colleges & universities · EdTech & online learning

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Department offices and support teams answer the same questions about exam forms, hostel rules, scholarships, certificates and refunds all term. Answers vary by who replies, and serious messages about harassment, ragging or distress can sit in the same inbox as routine queries.

Trigger

A student, parent or learner sends a question to the helpdesk WhatsApp number, the student portal or the in-app help widget.

How it runs

  • Screen every message first for ragging, harassment, self-harm or emergency words agreed with the owner; on a match, alert the named person at once and show the National Anti-Ragging Helpline, 1800-180-5522, or Tele-MANAS, 14416.
  • Classify the rest into topics such as exams, fees, hostel, scholarships, certificates, login or refunds.
  • Answer only from the approved handbook, policy and help center documents, citing the section used; low-confidence answers are not sent.
  • Hand grievances to the institution's grievance channel, account-specific requests to the right office, and anything unanswered to a staffed queue with a summary.
  • Flag questions the documents could not answer so owners can update them, and re-index changed documents the same day.

Human checkpoint

The dean of students or learner success lead owns the sensitive-message rules and the staffed queue. Ragging reports go to the Anti-Ragging Committee and grievances to the Students' Grievance Redressal Committee; fee waivers, discipline and academic exceptions are decided only by the authorized office.

Conversations are kept for the period the institution sets, and model calls run under enterprise terms without training use.

What we deliver

  • Sensitive-message routing approved by the dean of students
  • Staffed queue with response-time alerts
  • Monthly content gap report

How we measure it

  • Questions answered with a cited source
  • Sensitive messages acknowledged by a person within the agreed time
  • Handoff rate by topic
  • Unanswered questions turned into document updates

Attend and learnStandard3–5 weeks

Course progress nudges and cohort engagement

Learners who stall get a reminder tied to their next module or live session, cohorts get session and deadline reminders, and learners who stay inactive are flagged to a mentor instead of receiving more messages. Child accounts get parent-facing summaries only.

EdTech & online learning

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Completion falls after the first modules, live cohort attendance drops mid-course, and blanket reminder emails get ignored or unsubscribed. Mentors cannot easily tell which learners need a personal call, and learners under eighteen cannot be profiled for engagement nudges.

Trigger

A learner misses a planned module or assignment, a live session or deadline approaches, or an adult learner stays inactive for the period the team sets.

How it runs

  • Compute each adult learner's progress against the cohort plan from course platform events, and only completion status for child accounts.
  • Send live session and assignment deadline reminders on the channel each learner chose, with a weekly message cap.
  • For adults who stall, send one nudge tied to the next module, with a link back to where they left off.
  • After repeated inactivity, stop automated nudges and create a mentor task with the learner's progress summary.
  • Send parents of under-18 learners a weekly progress summary and session schedule, with no behavior-based targeting.
  • Report completion, attendance and mentor outreach by cohort and course.

Human checkpoint

Mentors decide whom to call and what support to offer, and the learning lead approves caps and wording. Extensions, deferrals and refunds are decided by the learner success lead under the published policy.

  • Mentor task queue

Assess and reportAdvanced5–7 weeks

Test analytics and doubt routing to faculty

Each mock test produces a private topic and time analysis against the student's own history for the student, parent and mentor. Doubts sent as photos or text are tagged by subject and chapter and queued to the right faculty, with similar solved questions attached.

Coaching & test-prep institutes · EdTech & online learning

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Test results show marks and ranks but not which topics or habits cost marks. Doubts sent by photo in crowded groups wait days or reach the wrong teacher, and mentors notice a struggling student only after several poor tests.

Trigger

Results of a mock or practice test are published from the test platform or OMR scanner, or a student submits a doubt in the app, portal or doubt WhatsApp number.

How it runs

  • Import question-level responses and compute accuracy and time by subject, chapter and difficulty, compared with the student's previous tests.
  • Publish a private analysis to the student and, for minors, the parent, with practice sets from the institute's own question bank and no public rank lists.
  • Alert the student's mentor when scores drop sharply or tests are missed, with the analysis attached for a conversation.
  • Read submitted doubt photos or text, tag subject, chapter and question type, and attach similar solved questions from the institute's bank.
  • Queue each doubt to the right faculty or doubt solver with a response target; faculty may start from an AI-drafted hint that they edit before sending.
  • Report doubt volume, resolution time and recurring weak topics to the academic head for remedial classes.

Human checkpoint

Faculty answer every doubt and approve any drafted hint before it reaches a student. Mentors decide on counseling or extra classes, and any sign of stress or distress goes to the institute's counselor, never to an automated message.

Tools

Systems it connects

  • Online test platform or OMR scanning software
  • Question bank and solutions library
  • Coaching ERP or course platform

Data & consent

Uses responses, scores and doubts only for the student's own academic support. For minors, parental consent is recorded and analysis stays within the educational purpose the DPDP Rules exempt, as the legal owner confirms. Analyses are private to the student, parent and assigned staff, never used for advertising or profiling, and deleted or anonymized after the retention period.

What we deliver

  • Question-level test analytics pipeline
  • Private student and parent reports
  • Doubt queue with subject routing
  • Weak-topic dashboard for academic heads

How we measure it

  • Doubt resolution time
  • Doubts answered by the right subject faculty first time
  • Mentor reviews after a sharp score drop
  • Weak topics covered in remedial classes
